reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard rheumatology references
clinicalPearls: A group of disorders characterised by sterile (culture-negative) inflammation of bone driven by innate immune dysregulation rather than infection
The spectrum spans sporadic chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis (including CRMO), the adult SAPHO syndrome, and rare monogenic forms
Deficiency of the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA), caused by IL1RN mutations, presents in neonates with sterile multifocal osteomyelitis, periostitis, and pustular skin disease
Majeed syndrome, due to LPIN2 mutations, combines chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis with congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia and a neutrophilic dermatosis
Bone pain, local swelling, and multifocal metaphyseal or clavicular lesions are typical, often with a relapsing course
Interleukin-1 signalling is central to many of these conditions, and IL-1 blockade is dramatically effective in the monogenic IL-1-driven forms such as DIRA
MRI (including whole-body imaging) detects clinically silent lesions, and biopsy shows sterile inflammation with negative cultures
The diagnosis rests on excluding infection and malignancy and recognising associated skin, gut, or haematological features
reference.pathophysiology: These conditions arise from dysregulated innate immunity leading to sterile osteoclast- and neutrophil-mediated bone inflammation. In monogenic forms, specific defects drive the phenotype: loss of the IL-1 receptor antagonist (DIRA) removes the natural brake on IL-1 signalling, producing unopposed IL-1-mediated inflammation, while LPIN2 mutations (Majeed syndrome) disturb lipid metabolism and inflammatory regulation. The common theme is cytokine-driven (especially IL-1) sterile osteitis with reactive bone remodelling.
additionalDifferentials: Other systemic autoinflammatory syndromes with bone involvement
additionalInvestigations: Whole-body MRI to define multifocal and subclinical lesions
Bone biopsy with microbiology and histology to confirm sterile inflammation
Targeted genetic testing (e.g. IL1RN, LPIN2) in early-onset or syndromic presentations
Full blood count to detect anaemia or dyserythropoiesis (as in Majeed syndrome)
redFlags: Features indistinguishable from bacterial osteomyelitis or malignancy without biopsy
Vertebral lesions risking collapse, deformity, or neurological compromise
Neonatal presentation with severe systemic inflammation suggesting a monogenic IL-1-driven disorder
Progressive anaemia or cytopenias pointing to a syndromic (e.g. Majeed) form
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies by subtype: sporadic nonbacterial osteomyelitis often follows a fluctuating course that eventually settles, whereas monogenic IL-1-driven forms can be severe in infancy but respond dramatically to IL-1 blockade; early recognition and treatment limit permanent skeletal damage.
pitfalls: Treating sterile osteitis as bacterial infection with repeated or prolonged antibiotics
Failing to consider a monogenic cause in neonatal or syndromic presentations
Underusing whole-body imaging and underestimating disease extent
Missing associated skin, gut, or haematological disease that clarifies the diagnosis
management: First-line non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for sporadic chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis and CRMO
Escalation to bisphosphonates, TNF inhibitors, or corticosteroids with methotrexate or sulfasalazine for NSAID-refractory, spinal or erosive disease
Interleukin-1 blockade with anakinra as targeted therapy, dramatically effective in the monogenic IL-1-driven forms such as DIRA
Supportive analgesia and physiotherapy to preserve function and limit skeletal deformity
Whole-body MRI surveillance to monitor multifocal and subclinical lesions and gauge treatment response
Management of associated features, including congenital dyserythropoietic anaemia in Majeed syndrome and neutrophilic skin disease
Targeted genetic testing (IL1RN, LPIN2) with genetic counselling in early-onset or syndromic presentations
Multidisciplinary rheumatology, orthopaedics and dermatology care
